headline_marked: BNP MP Ferdousy Ahmed [[ordered to resign]] over Radda health centre attack
headline: BNP MP Ferdousy Ahmed ordered to resign over Radda health centre attack
summary: The reserved-seat lawmaker was instructed to step down following allegations of her involvement in the looting and vandalism of a Mirpur health centre.
details: BNP reserved-seat lawmaker Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti has been ordered to resign from parliament following an attack, looting, and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1.
The Prime Minister's Press Secretary, Abu Abdullah M Saleh, confirmed that Mishti was instructed to resign by Sunday.
The incident occurred around midnight on September 24, when the health centre's premises were demolished and looted.
While local BNP and affiliated organization leaders have been named in connection with the attack, Mishti has denied any involvement in the incident.
She further stated she has no current association with the Somomona Dokandar Samabaya Samity Limited, a group involved in a land dispute over the centre's location.
An investigation is currently underway, with Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stating that no one would be spared if evidence of involvement is found.
In a related development, the 51-member convening committee of Dhaka North BNP, of which Mishti was a joint convenor, has been dissolved.
caption:
A BNP lawmaker has been ordered to resign after a health centre in Mirpur was looted and demolished.

BNP reserved-seat lawmaker Ferdousy Ahmed Mishti has been ordered to resign from parliament following an attack, looting, and vandalism at the Radda MCH-FP Centre in Mirpur-1.

The Prime Minister's Press Secretary, Abu Abdullah M Saleh, confirmed that Mishti was instructed to resign by Sunday.

The incident occurred around midnight on September 24, when the health centre's premises were demolished and looted.

While local BNP and affiliated organization leaders have been named in connection with the attack, Mishti has denied any involvement in the incident.

She further stated she has no current association with the Somomona Dokandar Samabaya Samity Limited, a group involved in a land dispute over the centre's location.

An investigation is currently underway, with Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stating that no one would be spared if evidence of involvement is found.

In a related development, the 51-member convening committee of Dhaka North BNP, of which Mishti was a joint convenor, has been dissolved.

Source: Jamuna TV, bdnews24.com, Dhaka Tribune, Prothom Alo, The Daily Star

headline: 3 DNCC trucks set on fire during Mirpur eviction drive
summary: Police have filed four cases and arrested 26 people following violent clashes between hawkers and city officials during a footpath clearing operation.
details: Three Dhaka North City Corporation (DNCC) trucks were set on fire and an excavator and a police vehicle were vandalised during a violent eviction drive in Mirpur.
The clashes erupted after DNCC officials attempted to clear illegal structures and hawker stalls from the footpaths around Mirpur-10.
A case has been filed with Kafrul Police Station against 400-500 unidentified people following the violence.
According to police, four cases have been filed in total and 26 people have been arrested so far.
The confrontation involved chases and counter-chases between hawkers, police, and DNCC officials.
Authorities are continuing their efforts to identify and arrest those involved in the attacks on government vehicles.
